title: Why are the two angles made by the crease equal?
description: The crease OC splits the straight angle AOB into two angles. Folding along OC puts OB exactly on OA, so one angle lands exactly on the other, and this is the reason they are equal. Keeko's doubt is that the angles look equal, so no check is needed.
teaching_notes: One idea: folding along the crease is itself a superimposition, and the angles that fit exactly on each other are equal. Watch for students who rely on how the angles look.

source: Justify why the two angles are equal. Is there a way to supe

folding along OC puts OB exactly on OA, so the two arms coincide

angles that fit exactly on each other are equal
